summary: Over the last 4 weeks, training volume has been low with only 9 sessions logged, heavily weighted toward cycling and open-water swimming, and no running recorded at all — a significant gap with a 10K race 22 days away. Sleep quality is a concern, with many nights under 5 hours and body battery frequently in the 12–55 range, suggesting accumulated fatigue and insufficient recovery. The Half Oceanman swim in 14 days is the immediate priority, and recent open-water swim efforts at 160–161 bpm suggest the athlete is working at high intensity during swims, which needs to ease into race-pace control this week.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else this week — body battery has been critically low (as low as 12) on multiple days, and arriving at the Half Oceanman under-recovered will hurt performance far more than any additional training session.

The complete absence of running over the last 4 weeks is a red flag for the Treviso 10K in 22 days — introduce short, easy runs (20–30 min at 6:45–7:00/km) this week and next to re-activate running legs without adding injury risk.

Swim HR has consistently been at 160–161 bpm during open-water sessions; shift this week's remaining swim work toward controlled aerobic effort (target HR ≤145 bpm) to practice the pacing discipline required for a 5,000m race event.

The planned 120km ride on Sep 26 (Wk14, 17 days before the Half Oceanman) is aggressive given the low recent training load — cap it at 80km and remove the Z3 tempo blocks to avoid digging a fatigue hole heading into the race.

Post-Half Oceanman (Oct 3+), allow 2–3 days of full rest before resuming any running load — racing a 5,000m open-water swim will leave the shoulders and aerobic system taxed, and the Treviso 10K is only 7 days later.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk13 Long Ride (AI adjusted): 60km @ 120–145W, cap at 120 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 45–60 min easy spin at 120–140W (Z2 only), flat route, HR ≤130 bpm, no distance target — body battery today is critically low (max 7) and sleep data is absent, so any meaningful load risks compounding fatigue 14 days out from the Half Oceanman.
proposed_changes.reason: Today's body battery peaked at just 7 and no sleep was recorded, indicating the athlete is in a deeply fatigued state — a long ride today would be counterproductive 14 days before the Half Oceanman.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk13 Long Run (AI adjusted): 10–12km @ 6:45–7:00/km, cap at 75 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 20–25 min easy jog at 7:00–7:15/km, flat, HR ≤125 bpm, stop early if legs feel heavy — this is a re-introduction run after 4+ weeks of no running, not a fitness session.
proposed_changes.reason: No running has been logged in the last 4 weeks; jumping to 10–12km risks injury and the athlete needs leg re-awakening at minimal load, not a long run, 13 days before the Half Oceanman and 22 days before the 10K.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Evening session: 5x5min @ 210–244W (Z4 Threshold), 3min Z1 recovery, 60–75 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip the threshold intervals entirely — replace with 40 min easy Z2 spin at 128–155W, flat and steady, HR ≤135 bpm, to keep legs ticking without adding intensity stress 8 days before the Half Oceanman.
proposed_changes.reason: High-intensity Z4 intervals 8 days before a priority race are counterproductive and will leave residual fatigue in the legs — aerobic maintenance is sufficient at this point in the taper.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Long Ride: 120km @ 128–177W (Z2), optional 3x10min Z3 Tempo blocks
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cap at 80km @ 128–155W (Z2 only, lower end), no tempo blocks, stop if HR drifts above 140 bpm — this is the final long stimulus before the Half Oceanman and must not leave the athlete depleted.
proposed_changes.reason: A 120km ride 6 days before the Half Oceanman exceeds safe taper volume given the athlete's low recent training load; 80km at easy Z2 provides aerobic maintenance without compromising race-day freshness.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 30–35 min easy run at 6:45–7:00/km, flat, HR ≤130 bpm — a gentle second running re-introduction session to keep legs active ahead of the Treviso 10K without adding load 5 days before the Half Oceanman.
proposed_changes.reason: A 21km long run 5 days before the Half Oceanman is excessive and would leave the athlete fatigued for the swim race; with zero running in the past 4 weeks, a short easy run is both safer and more appropriate.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 20–25 min very easy recovery jog at 7:00–7:30/km the day after the Half Oceanman, or full rest if shoulders/body feel beaten up — do not attempt 21.5km; the Treviso 10K is only 6 days away and the body needs to recover from racing 5,000m open water.
proposed_changes.reason: Racing 5,000m open water the day before makes a 21.5km long run the next day a serious injury and overtraining risk, especially with the Treviso 10K just 6 days later.
